items.basis: Thermal diffusion is a physical process inappropriate for recommendation signals which are discrete preferences, not continuous quantities that can diffuse; the candidate fails to address the fundamental categorical nature of user preferences.

No boundary conditions provided for when thermal equilibrium would be appropriate versus when maintaining diversity should take precedence; critical for a system where content popularity dynamics change rapidly.

The provided evidence includes papers on GNSS trajectory consistency and BERT sentiment analysis which are entirely unrelated to recommendation system feedback loops, demonstrating the candidate lacks relevant foundational research.

The mechanism fails to address the core feedback loop problem as it only redistributes existing recommendations rather than breaking the cycle of training on past outputs; it will inevitably recreate the same diversity collapse.
There is no defined method to translate abstract "temperature" metrics into concrete recommendation adjustments, making the mechanism impossible to implement in practice.
The prediction fails to define how "temperature variance" will be calculated in a recommendation context where there is no natural thermal metric, making the testable prediction meaningless.
